story: Apple contractors listened to 1k Siri recordings per shift: former employee
text: All of that sounds impressive, until you see red team pros talk about how the whole apparatus melts before the gentlest of social engineering- [VIDEO] I'd also be concerned with leaking of mass amounts of records at once due to a security lapse on servers where it's a bit easier for grossly inadequate protections to lurk unnoticed- [LINK] I think I've read that Google doesn't even store the original recordings, but distorts them randomly to make them unrecognizable but still intelligible by their models. That seems like a pretty reasonable way to protect people, provided they're informed and there's no link back to the original account.

They do do that, if I understand correctly. Penetration testing handles the physical security of the company. [DEFCON 19: Steal Everything, Kill Everyone, Cause Total Financial Ruin! ]( [VIDEO] ) Social Engineering [Hacking the Wetware: Compromising Companies with Social Engineering]( [LINK] )
